newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine truck drivers launch protest.
newsitem.headline: Argentine truck drivers launch protest.

text.p: Argentine truck drivers began a three-day protest on Sunday against competition from foreign transportation companies, heading out from the western province of Mendoza for a 621 mile (1,000 km) ride to Buenos Aires province.
More than 1,000 trucks carrying petrol, gas, livestock, cereal, fruit and vegetables formed a 12-mile (20-km) -long caravan on national highway 7 bound for Lujan, Buenos Aires.
The National Truck Drivers Federation said the protest was called "to defend the national transportation industry and the dignity of truck workers."
It predicted as many as 2,500 trucks will have joined the caravan by the time it reaches Lujan.
The protest, which includes road blockades, could affect food supplies in the capital and greater Buenos Aires area.

"With this government which is deaf, blind and mute regarding the labor situation, the only way to make our demands heard is to protest like we are doing now," truck drivers union leader Hugo Moyano said.
He threatened to call a 14-day strike that would block the country's border crossings.
"It's not the first or the last time we take to the roads," said Moyano.
Last December angry truck drivers cut off three border passes in Corrientes, Misiones and Mendoza provinces.
